CRM.rationale: Salesforce delivered a strong Q1 FY2027 with revenue of $11.13B (+13% YoY), GAAP EPS of $2.42 (+52% YoY), and non-GAAP EPS of $3.88 (+50% YoY), beating consensus on both lines. Operating cash flow was $6.7B and GAAP operating margin expanded to 21.1%. The company raised its full-year FY27 revenue guidance midpoint to $46.05B (~11% growth). Agentforce ARR crossed $1.2B (+205% YoY), signaling genuine AI monetization traction. However, the stock has declined ~30% YTD to $176.17, compressing the P/E to 19.1x — the lowest in the 12-month window (range 19.1–57.6x) and well below the 1-year average of ~47x. This represents a significant re-rating vs. own history, driven by SaaS-sector AI disruption fears and soft Q2 revenue guidance ($11.27–11.35B vs. $11.36B consensus). Balance sheet leverage increased meaningfully post-Informatica acquisition (debt-to-equity 1.15x vs. 0.14x a year ago), and management acknowledged ongoing weakness in Tableau bookings and marketing/commerce. The near-term catalyst is the Q1 earnings beat just reported (May 27), which should provide a floor, though the stock was down 1.86% post-earnings on soft guidance. The combination of accelerating AI monetization, record profitability, aggressive buybacks ($27.5B returned in Q1 including $25B ASR), and historically compressed valuation creates a moderately attractive setup, tempered by legitimate concerns about SaaS model disruption risk and elevated leverage.

Salesforce reported its first $11.1 billion quarter with strong metrics including $6.7 billion operating cash flow and a 152% increase in processed tokens. However, the stock declined after the company provided Q2 revenue guidance of $11.27-$11.35 billion, slightly below analyst expectations.

Revenue increased 13% year over year. Net income rose to $2.11 billion, or $2.42 per share, from $1.54 billion, or $1.59 per share, a year earlier. Annualized revenue from Agentforce reached $1.2 billion, up 205% year over year. RPO stood at $67.9 billion vs $68.61B consensus.

GAAP EPS $2.42, up 52% Y/Y, Non-GAAP EPS $3.88, up 50% Y/Y. First quarter revenue of $11.1 billion, up 13% Y/Y. Returned $27.5 billion to shareholders, including $27.1 billion in share repurchases and $365 million in dividends.
AI disruption fears pressure SaaS sector and CRM stock. Slack sues Microsoft for alleged anticompetitive practices. Investors reduced stakes; analysts lowered price targets.
At US$181.32, Salesforce trades about 32% below the US$268.25 analyst target. Simply Wall St estimates the shares are trading roughly 47.4% below fair value.

Management cited ongoing weakness in marketing and commerce and increased softness in Tableau bookings and renewals affecting guidance. Recent debt issuance tied to ASR resulted in approximately 5-point headwind to operating cash flow.
